name: CR-Int-13-parts-4.a
questiontext:
Evaluate the following definite integral:
\[ \int^{{CT:0}}_{{CT:1}} {{CT:2}} d{{CT:3}}. \]

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]
generalfeedback:
If \[\int f(x) dx = F(x)\] then
\[\int^a_b f(x) dx = F(a) - F(b).\]

Using integration by parts,
\[\int u dv = uv - \int v du,\]
by defining \(u = {{CT:4}}\) and \(dv = {{CT:5}} d{{CT:3}}\) so that

\(du = {{CT:6}} d{{CT:3}}\) and \(v = {{CT:7}}\).

Then,

\[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle
 \int {{CT:2}} d{{CT:3}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  \int u dv \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  uv - \int v du \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:4}}{{CT:7}} - \int {{CT:7}}{{CT:6}} d{{CT:3}}
 \end{array}\]

To calculate \[\int {{CT:8}}d{{CT:3}}\] we will have to use parts again, by defining

\(u = {{CT:6}}\) and \(dv = {{CT:7}}d{{CT:3}}\) so that

\(du = {{CT:9}}d{{CT:3}}\) and \(v = {{CT:10}}\).

So,

\[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle
 \int {{CT:8}}d{{CT:3}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  \int u dv \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  uv - \int v du \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:6}}[{{CT:10}}] - \int [{{CT:10}}]{{CT:9}}d{{CT:3}} \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:11}} - \int {{CT:12}}d{{CT:3}} \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:13}}
 \end{array}\]

Hence,

\[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle
 \int {{CT:2}} d{{CT:3}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:14}} - ({{CT:13}}) \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:15}} \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:16}}
 \end{array}\]

Lastly, we evaluate this expression at the limits to give

\[ \left[{{CT:17}}\right]_{{CT:1}}^{{CT:0}} = {{CT:18}}.\]

on_true.feedback: This is a definite integration problem, so your answer should be a number.  This is the correct integral, but you have not evaluated it.
